definition: A status word in a pill. The only component that puts role-coloured text on a role-coloured tint, so the surface underneath it changes what the pairing measures.
reachForItWhen: A render finished or failed and the row has to say which without the user opening the clip
One column of a table carries the same kind of fact in every row — state, plan tier, model
A queue item is waiting and the word has to change under the user's eyes when it starts
A count, quota or version sits beside a heading with no room to become a sentence
A feature is new and the nav item has to say so for the fortnight that stays true

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The word is clickable — it filters the list, clears the tag or opens the failure
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Button. `BadgeProps` extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>`, so an `onClick` type-checks and spreads onto the `<span>` — arriving with no tabstop, no ring and no 44px target.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The status needs a sentence — what failed, and what the user does next
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Alert. Same `surface/<role>` tint, body set in `content/secondary` at `text-body-sm` (`Alert.tsx:43`); the pill has no second line to put it on.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The user writes the state rather than reads it — a setting they can turn off
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Switch. A badge reports what the system decided; a switch is the decision. A pill that changes when clicked is a switch wearing the wrong component.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The value has not arrived and the layout slot still has to hold its width
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Skeleton, which reserves the box and pulses. There is no loading variant here and none is coming — a badge is a resolved fact or it is absent.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: Every cell in the column would get one, so the pills outnumber the words
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Table. Put the value in the cell as text; a state column is findable only while it is the one column with colour in it.

variants.useWhen: Metadata with no valence — a model name, a count, a plan tier. The default, and the only variant with no cap, because it spends nothing from the screen's colour budget.
variants.avoidWhen: On a `surface/secondary` panel. The pill fill is that same token — 1.000:1 against its own bed in both modes — and the badge draws no border, so there is no boundary at all. The word holds at 11.91:1 in light and 9.06:1 in dark while the pill around it stops existing, which turns a status into loose text. Move it to a card or the page.

variants.useWhen: The thing is new, in beta, or ours: "New" beside a model heading. At most one per view — it draws on the accent `button.recipe.ts` already caps at one primary per view.
variants.avoidWhen: A brand badge is already on screen, or the word names an outcome. Two orange objects and the eye stops finding the action; "Ready" is a finished state, which is success.

variants.useWhen: A finished, good outcome the user can act on now: "Ready", "Complete", "Paid". At most one status badge per object.
variants.avoidWhen: The work is still running. A green "Rendering" promises a result that has not arrived and the user opens the row to collect it — that state is info.

variants.useWhen: Nothing is broken, something will break, and the user still holds a lever: "82% of quota", "Expires in 3 days". One per object, and the object still works.
variants.avoidWhen: The user cannot change the outcome. A warning with no lever is an outcome, and an outcome is success, critical or neutral.

variants.useWhen: Failed or blocked, and the row carries the action that clears it: "Failed". One per object, and it is the variant that earns a scan of the whole column.
variants.avoidWhen: The state is closed and nothing can be done — a cancelled job, an expired trial. Red on a finished list reads as a queue of work, and the user opens every red row to find nothing in it. Use neutral.

variants.useWhen: A system state that is still moving: "Queued", "Rendering", "Scheduled". One per object, and the variant a badge changes away from rather than toward.
variants.avoidWhen: The value is permanent metadata. "Seedance 2" never becomes "Ready", so it is neutral — info is the blue that means wait.

guidance.useWhen: The text beside it is set at the 12px label step or smaller — a table cell, a nav item, a row of chips.
The badge sits beside a heading or body copy, which is everywhere a badge is not inside a dense row.

sizes.note: Two sizes, and the type step of the neighbouring text selects between them — never the urgency of the status. `sm` sets its label at 10px, the smallest of the fifteen steps in the scale; `md` sets it at the same 12px a Button `sm` label uses, so a badge beside a small button is set to match it. There is no `lg`, because the next step up is 14px (`text-label-md`), the default Button label — a badge set exactly like a button label with no tabstop and no 44px target reads as a control that is not one. Mixing sizes down a column is what breaks: an `md` badge dropped into a run of `sm` rows makes that one row taller than its neighbours, and a table where every fifth row is taller reads as a rendering fault rather than as emphasis.

copy: Label copy — the only author-supplied string this component renders:
name the state as it is now, not the event that reached it: "Ready", never "Render finished"
cap at three words carrying one fact: "82% of quota", never "82% of your monthly render quota"
keep a number with its subject: "82% of quota", never a bare "82%"
write sentence case: "New", never "NEW" — the two label steps ship at 10px and 12px with tracking already applied, and all-caps at 10px is the least legible pair in the scale
take no terminal punctuation and no exclamation mark: "New", never "New!"
reject "Error" — it names the category the column already names; "Failed" names what happened to this clip
reject "OK" — an outcome word with no object; "Ready" says the clip can be played
reject "Active" — it reads as both "currently running" and "not cancelled"; pick "Rendering" or "Enabled" and mean one of them
reject "Model timed out after 90 seconds" — that is an Alert body, and the pill does not wrap
Dot copy: none. The dot renders no string and carries `aria-hidden="true"` in `Badge.tsx`, so the label rules above are the whole copy contract for this component.
motion: A badge appears because something changed — a render finished, a queue moved — so it arrives with a small scale-up rather than materialising; a fade alone lets a status flip past unnoticed. When only the variant changes under a mounted pill the colour crossfades and nothing moves: a bounce there is a physical claim about a word that has not moved. There is no press response, deliberately — a pill that answers the pointer teaches the user it can be pressed.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: Dark mode, the badge placed deeper than a card
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Refuse below `surface/secondary`. The tint is a 15%-alpha token in dark, so it composites with its bed: `content/<role>` on `surface/<role>` measures 5.93–6.14:1 on the page, 5.26–5.45:1 on `surface/primary` and 4.60–4.79:1 on `surface/secondary`, then falls to 3.93–4.08:1 on `surface/tertiary` and 3.42–3.55:1 on `surface/elevated` — under the 4.5 floor on all five status roles for the last two. Measured 2026-08-02 with `contrast()` and `composite()` from `build/palette.mjs`. Light is bed-invariant at 6.24–7.47:1 because the tint is opaque there, so this fails in exactly one mode and only for whoever is running it.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: A label long enough to widen the pill — a model name, or "Rendering" doubled by translation
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Grow. `whitespace-nowrap` is in the shape, so the pill widens and never wraps, and the row reflows around it. The one string that earns `.oz-truncate` is a user-supplied value in the neutral variant — a model name, a filename — and it needs `min-width: 0` on the parent flex or grid child, which `dist/layout.css` already ships on its primitives, or `text-overflow` does nothing at all.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: The status changes while the user is looking at the row
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Crossfade in place, silently. The element does not re-mount, so the entrance does not replay and only the colour moves. `Badge` renders a bare `<span>` with no `role` and no `aria-live`, so a pill flipping from "Queued" to "Failed" announces nothing — the live region belongs on the container that owns the row and says "Clip 3 failed", not on the eleven elements inside it. `{...rest}` spreads onto the `<span>`, so the component does not block one either.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: The consuming app's Tailwind config carries no safelist
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: The dot disappears and the label survives. `Badge.tsx` composes the dot's class at runtime as `bg-fill-${variant}`, so it exists only because of the `^bg-(fill|surface|sidebar|background)(-|$)` pattern in `tailwind.config.js`; without it the class is emitted into the HTML, matches no CSS rule, and the badge renders a 6px transparent gap before the word.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: There is no status to show
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Render nothing. There is no empty state and no zero-height variant: an empty pill is 8px or 12px of horizontal padding either side of zero characters, so it renders as a 16px or 24px lozenge of bare `surface/<role>` tint, which a user reads as a fault rather than as an absence.
The pill widens; it neither wraps nor truncates. When a row loses content at 200%, the defect is a fixed-width column around the badge and not the badge — WCAG 1.4.4.

enforced.claim: Every colour token the six bindings name resolves in both modes.
enforced.assertion: the `bindingRoles` existence sweep at the head of `showcase/scripts/verify-contrast.ts`, run by `npm run verify`

enforced.claim: `content/<role>` on `surface/<role>` clears 4.5:1 for all six variants in both modes — measured over the page and nowhere else.
enforced.assertion: the per-variant WCAG sweep in `showcase/scripts/verify-contrast.ts`, whose `flatten()` composites every translucent token over `resolve('background', mode)`. It passes this component at 5.93–6.14:1 dark; see `notEnforced` for what that number is not.

enforced.claim: A `spatial-*` spring on the badge's colour transition fails the build.
The dot's runtime-composed class matches a real CSS rule.
enforced.assertion: `showcase/scripts/verify-classes.mjs`, which diffs the prerendered HTML against the compiled stylesheet — the showcase's own output only, never a consumer's

enforced.claim: The badge cannot ship without a stated reason for how it moves.
enforced.assertion: check 1 of `showcase/scripts/verify-motion.ts` fails a `motion.intent` under eight words; `motion` is additionally `abstract readonly` on `ComponentRecipe`, so a recipe without one does not compile

enforced.claim: A seventh variant cannot be added without answering the focus question.
enforced.assertion: `focus: FocusMode` is a required field on `VariantBinding` in `showcase/lib/core/types.ts`. `'none'` is a stated answer, not an omission — the mistake is unexpressible rather than caught.

notEnforced: The bed. Every gate that touches this component flattens the tint over `color/background`, so the four surfaces a badge can actually sit on are invisible to all of them. The two deepest fail 4.5:1 in dark and nothing reports it. The human check is to measure with `contrast()` and `composite()` from `build/palette.mjs` against the surface the badge really sits on.

The pill's edge. The badge draws no border, so the `surface/<role>` tint is the only thing dividing it from what it sits on, and nothing measures that. `VISIBILITY_ASSERTIONS` in `build/spec.mjs` holds six pairs — five of them a border against a surface, the sixth `surface/primary` against the page — and no `surface/<role>` against any bed a badge lands on. The worst case is the neutral pill on a `surface/secondary` panel at 1.000:1, and the build reports that badge as passing.

The dot's greyscale separation. `CHART_MIN_DL` in `build/build.mjs` is 0.05 and is applied to `color/chart/1..5` only. Run against the five status dot fills it would fail seven of the ten pairs, three of them below ΔL 0.002.

A click handler. `BadgeProps` extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>`, so `onClick`, `tabIndex` and `role` type-check and spread onto the `<span>`. Nothing in the type system, the token build or `showcase/scripts/` sees a badge that has become a control.
Scarcity. Nothing counts badges per view, per object or per column. Every cap on this page is a review step, not a gate.
The accessible name. Nothing measures whether the label is a complete status once the colour is gone. The human check is to desaturate a screenshot of the status column and read it top to bottom.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: On a neutral badge the dot nearly vanishes, while the same dot on every other variant reads at a glance.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: `fill/tertiary` is `#E3E1E0` on an `#EFEDEC` pill in light, so a neutral dot measures 1.117:1 against the tint it sits on; in dark the pair is `#2E2C2B` on `#211F1D` and measures 1.182:1. The five coloured dots measure 3.11–3.90:1 in light and 4.09–5.05:1 in dark against their own tints. Correct: neutral carries no valence to signal, and a visible dot on it would be a status marker on a badge that reports no status. Turn the dot off on neutral.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: A contrast check on the pill against the page comes back at 1.123–1.152:1 in light, and the badge draws no border to make up the difference.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: The tint separates by chroma and a contrast ratio reads only luminance, so the instrument cannot see the thing doing the work. In light the five status tints sit at L* 95.3–96.1 against a page at L* 100 — four points — and carry C 0.0198–0.0276 where the neutral pill beside them carries C 0.0025. WCAG 1.4.11 reaches non-text objects that carry meaning; a pill boundary is not one, because the word carries the status and `content/<role>` on `surface/<role>` clears 4.5:1 over the page in both modes. Six borders came off this component when the stroke policy landed, and the twenty-one that survive across seven variants are all `affordance`, which a badge edge is not.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: The badge still animates for a user who set `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: Only the fade does. The entrance's scale term is written through the multiplier and collapses to 1 while the opacity ramp survives — the graded tier legislated in DECISIONS.md B16 and listed in CLAUDE.md, which the badge neither overrides nor needs to. The crossfade between variants survives with it, so a pill going from "Queued" to "Failed" marks the change for that user rather than swapping colour between two frames.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: A target-size audit flags the `sm` badge: it is far under 44px and shows no focus indicator.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: Correct, and both are the same fact. WCAG 2.5.8 and 2.4.7 reach targets and focusable elements; a badge is neither. All six bindings declare `focus: 'none'`, the recipe binds no hover and no active, and the `<span>` takes no tabstop. The moment a badge acquires an `onClick` all three become real defects at once — which is the same sentence as: it is a Button.

related.difference: When one message covers many objects rather than one per object. An Alert speaks for the batch — what happened and what to do next — and the badges say which three of the forty clips it was; one alert per failed row buries the fix under repetitions of the same sentence.

When the red proposes something rather than reports it. A badge's `critical` records the render that already failed; a button's `destructive` offers "Delete permanently", which has not happened yet — the same role colour, the opposite tense.

When the state has two positions and no third. A switch is `off` or `on` by construction, so a clip that is neither — "Rendering", between queued and ready — has nowhere to sit on a track, which is why there are six variants here and two there.
When the fact belongs to the row rather than to one object inside it. The row takes the interaction states and the badge becomes one cell of it.

When it is the object that is missing and not its status. `info` covers a state that is still moving, so a row already on screen has a word for it — a shimmer in that one cell reserves width for a value the system already knows.
A Badge inside a Card is metadata about the card; a Badge as the card is a card with one word in it. If it is the only content, the container is the wrong component.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — In dark, `surface/elevated` and `surface/overlay` moved to `neutral/105` (`#393735`, L* 33.8), and a badge in a popover or a dialog body became the worst bed in the system for this component: `content/<role>` on `surface/<role>` fell from 4.60–4.79:1 there to 3.42–3.55:1. The placement rule tightened to the page, `surface/primary` or `surface/secondary`, and no deeper.

Both floating surfaces previously sat at `neutral/120`, byte-identical to `surface/secondary`, so the tint composited over a darker bed and cleared 4.5:1 by luck. Every dark-bed figure on this page was recomputed on 2026-08-02 rather than carried over; a number measured before the move is wrong by roughly 1.2 ratio points.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — The neutral badge became visible on a floating surface. Its pill is `surface/secondary` (`#211F1D`), which was byte-identical to the old dark `surface/elevated` at 1.000:1; against `#393735` it now measures 1.386:1.
changed.why: DECISIONS.md B18. This is the one place the ladder move improved this component instead of degrading it, and it is why a popover no longer needs a border to stop a neutral pill dissolving into it.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — Contrast gates went 118 → 130, and none of the six new ones is the badge's pairing.
changed.why: DECISIONS.md B18b added `content/primary|secondary|tertiary` against `surface/elevated` and `surface/overlay`. `content/<role>` on `surface/<role>` still appears nowhere in `reports/audit.json` and is measured only by the showcase sweep, over the page. The count rising changes nothing in the `notEnforced` list above.

changed.why: DECISIONS.md B18c. The badge binds no disabled state and the dot reads `fill/<role>` at rest only. Recorded to close the question rather than because anything moved here.
